t.6.23.2: She beheld the eyes and the complexion of the face, that face so like her husband's, the hair and the line where the hair meets the brow, and that auspicious crest-jewel.
t.6.23.1: Sītā, having seen that head and that excellent bow, and bearing in mind the alliance with Sugrīva that Hanumān had told her of, began to lament.
t.6.23.3: Recognizing him by all these marks, deeply grieved, she then reproached Kaikeyī, wailing like a female osprey.
t.6.23.4: Be content, Kaikeyī, your desire fulfilled: slain is this joy of the family. The whole family has been destroyed by you, whose nature is given to strife.
t.6.23.5: What wrong, pray, had the noble Rāma done to Kaikeyī, that she sent him away from home to the forest clad in bark garments?
t.6.23.6: Having spoken thus, Vaidehī, the poor young woman, trembling and wretched, fell to the ground like a plantain tree that has been cut down.
t.6.23.7: After a moment she recovered and regained consciousness; then the long-eyed one, bending close to that head and smelling it, lamented.
t.6.23.8: Alas, I am undone, O mighty-armed one, I who faithfully followed your heroic vow! I have come upon this final state of yours, and I have been made a widow.
t.6.23.9: A husband's death before his wife is said to be a sign of her failing; yet you, a man of good conduct, have met your end before me, a woman of virtuous conduct.
t.6.23.10: I have passed from sorrow to sorrow and am sunk in an ocean of grief, and you, who had set out to rescue me, even you have been struck down.
t.6.23.11: O Rāghava, my mother-in-law Kausalyā, so loving, has been left bereft by you, her son, like a loving cow left without her calf by the calf itself.
t.6.23.12: O you of inconceivable prowess, those who foretold a long life for you spoke falsely, for you are short-lived, O Rāghava.
t.6.23.13: Or else, even though you are wise, your wisdom has perished; thus does Time ripen him, for Time is the source of all beings.
t.6.23.14: How is it that you, a knower of the science of policy, have met with an unforeseen death? For you knew the means of dealing with calamities and were skilled in avoiding them.
t.6.23.15: Thus you, lotus-eyed one, have been embraced and then torn away and carried off by me, a fierce and utterly cruel Kālarātri, the Night of Doom.
t.6.23.16: O mighty-armed one, forsaking me, this wretched woman, you lie upon the earth, O bull among men, as though upon a beloved and lovely woman.
t.6.23.17: O hero, here is your bow, adorned with gold and dear to me, which I always worshipped with care, offering perfumes and garlands.
t.6.23.18: O sinless one, surely you have now joined your father Daśaratha, my father-in-law, together with your ancestors of old in heaven.
t.6.23.19: Having become a star in heaven, you have accomplished a great and cherished deed; yet you disregard the holy lineage of royal sages, your own.
t.6.23.20: Why do you not look at me, O king? Why do you not answer me, your wife and companion, whom you won as a young girl when you yourself were young?
t.6.23.21: Remember, O Kākutstha, the promise you made while taking my hand, saying 'I shall walk the path of dharma with you'; take me, sorrowful as I am, along with you too.
t.6.23.22: Why, O best of those who walk the earth, have you abandoned me and gone from this world to the other world, leaving me here in sorrow?
t.6.23.23: That body of yours, which was accustomed to auspicious things and was embraced by me alone, is surely now being dragged about in all directions by flesh-eating beasts.
t.6.23.25: Of the three who had gone forth into exile, only one has come back; Kausalyā, consumed by grief, will question Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.23.24: You performed sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma, accompanied by ample gifts to the priests; why, then, will you not receive the funeral rite with the sacred agnihotra fire?
t.6.23.26: When she asks, he will surely tell her of the slaughter of your army of allies and of your own slaying by the rākṣasas in the night.
t.6.23.27: Hearing that you were slain while you slept, and that I was taken to the house of the rākṣasa, she will not survive, O Rāghava, her heart broken.
t.6.23.28: O Rāvaṇa, kindly strike me down at once upon Rāma's body; unite the husband with his wife, and so perform a most excellent good deed.
t.6.23.30: I heard it in my father's house from brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas: those women to whom their husband is dear attain worlds of great prosperity.
t.6.23.29: Join my head with his head and my body with his body; O Rāvaṇa, I shall follow the path of my great-souled husband. I do not wish to live even for a moment with one whose life is sinful.
t.6.23.31: He in whom dwell forbearance, self-restraint, generosity, truth, righteousness, gratitude, and non-violence toward all beings: without him, what refuge is there for me?
t.6.23.32: Thus the large-eyed daughter of Janaka, tormented by grief, lamented there, gazing upon her husband's head and bow.
t.6.23.33: While Sītā was lamenting thus, a rākṣasa from the army approached his master there with joined palms.
t.6.23.34: Saying, "Be victorious, noble son!", he saluted and propitiated him, and announced that Prahasta, the commander of the army, had arrived.
t.6.23.35: Prahasta has arrived together with all the ministers; there is some urgent business. Grant them an audience.
t.6.23.36: Having heard this, reported by the rākṣasa, Daśagrīva left the Aśoka grove and went to meet his ministers.
t.6.23.37: Having learned of Rāma's prowess, he deliberated with his ministers on all that he himself had to do, then entered the assembly hall and set it in motion.
t.6.23.38: But that head and that excellent bow vanished the very moment Rāvaṇa departed.
t.6.23.39: Then the lord of the Rākṣasas, together with those ministers of terrible valour, deliberated and settled upon a firm resolve regarding the matter of Rāma.
t.6.23.40: Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, who resembled Death itself, spoke to all the commanders of his forces, his well-wishers, who stood close by.
t.6.23.41: Quickly gather my armies with the roar of kettledrums struck loudly with drumsticks, and the reason is not to be told.
t.6.23.42: Then, accepting that command with the words "So be it," those army commanders gathered their own great host, and they reported to their lord, who was eager for battle, that it had assembled.
